analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: The page covers why a bill of rights was demanded during Constitution adoption debates, how the First Congress proposed 12 amendments, and how Articles 3 to 12 became 10 ratified amendments known as the Bill of Rights in 1791 with later notes on the remaining articles.

overview.headline: How 12 proposals became 10 ratified rights in 1791

keyPoints.point: The page notes 12 amendments originally proposed and 10 ratified as the Bill of Rights in 1791
keyPoints.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyPoints.point: opponents in adoption debates charged the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by central government
keyPoints.quote: During the debates on the adoption of the Constitution, its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government.

keyPoints.point: memory of British violation of civil rights before and during the Revolution shaped demands for protection
keyPoints.quote: Fresh in their minds was the memory of the British violation of civil rights before and during the Revolution.

keyPoints.point: state conventions in formal ratification asked for amendments with understanding they would be offered
keyPoints.quote: Several state conventions in their formal ratification of the Constitution asked for such amendments;

keyPoints.point: the First Congress proposed 12 amendments to the state legislatures on September 25, 1789 meeting frequent arguments
keyPoints.quote: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution

keyTerms.gloss: formal changes to the Constitution originally proposed to meet arguments raised against it
keyTerms.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyTerms.gloss: central government dominance opponents feared the Constitution as drafted would enable
keyTerms.quote: During the debates on the adoption of the Constitution, its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government.

keyTerms.gloss: individual citizens protections demanded to be spelled out in a bill of rights
keyTerms.quote: They demanded a "bill of rights" that would spell out the immunities of individual citizens.

keyTerms.gloss: formal approval action by state conventions that asked for amendments
keyTerms.quote: Several state conventions in their formal ratification of the Constitution asked for such amendments;

keyTerms.gloss: payment for services of Senators and Representatives subject to varying proposal
keyTerms.quote: Article 2 concerning “varying the compensation for the services of the Senators and Representatives” was finally ratified on May 7, 1992 as the 27th Amendment to the Constitution.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Connecting British violation memory to citizen demands and legislative action lets learners follow cause and effect in the order presented
componentPlan.focusQuote: Fresh in their minds was the memory of the British violation of civil rights before and during the Revolution.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Fact cards reinforce checkable details such as proposal and ratification dates and distinct fates of articles
componentPlan.focusQuote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments of the Constitution, known as the Bill of Rights.
